title: Prove coverage item by item
statement: Prove coverage by counting how many lessons and items serve each required skill, reading each scored item against the standard's boundary, and treat a zero as a gap.
example: All 82 sub-codes were covered at least once, but 61 of them were rated Low.
detail: A reading course closed 15 zero-coverage sub-codes to 0 in three verification passes, checking every closure against the code's exact assessment boundary by reading the actual scored item, not relabelling a slot (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/CURRICULUM-REVIEW-STANDING-2026-08-17.md`). A gap analysis the next day found all 82 sub-codes covered at least once but 61 of 82 rated Low, most with one item each (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-08-18.md`). Skills carried from an earlier grade were held out of placement, neither counted as coverage zeros nor fake-placed into slots they don't belong in (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/RULING-B-CARRIED-MASTERY.md`). Count from the current placements, and never put a skill in a slot it doesn't fit to close a gap.
against: a thin count need not be a gap: a whole-course thematic map calls thin cells the places where a thread rests at a grade and returns deeper later, a spiral rather than a checklist (`downloads/5.
